Berlin is expected to formally blame Moscow for the August drone attack at Leipzig/Halle Airport and pair the attribution with tougher national measures, more support for Ukraine and a major new EU sanctions package.
The shift is meant to mark an end to earlier restraint on Russian hybrid attacks.

France is ready to export its MdCN long-range naval cruise missile to Sweden for the first time, as part of a €4.3 billion deal for four French frigates built by Naval Group.
The MdCN is often described as the European equivalent of the U.S. Tomahawk, with a reported range of up to 1,400 km.
It has been used exclusively by the French Navy for nearly a decade and would now be supplied to a Northern European ally.
The deal would give Sweden a significant long-range deep-strike capability, alongside Aster 30 air-defense missiles and other weapons.
Source: Les Echos

🇺🇸🇮🇱 How US blinds the world to Israel's genocidal wars & its own strikes
One week after the US-Israeli war on Iran began, Planet Labs imposed a four-day delay on Gulf imagery. By early April, at the US government’s request, the freeze on high-resolution images became indefinite, with the newest usable commercial pictures of the region now dating March 9.
The official US rationale is that such imagery could help adversaries target American or allied forces. 
However, this smells more like censorship: 
🔴 A two-week delay might be enough to address the hypothetical risk – no apparent need for an open-ended ban 
🔴 Iran operates its own[ Earth Observation satellites](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/48590), like Khayyam, Pars-1, Zafar-2, and Paya (Tolou-3), launched on Russian Soyuz rockets
🔴 In May, Columbia Journalism Review found no evidence Iranian forces ever used imagery from any US satellite vendor
🔴 The Washington Post drew upon Iran’s own satellite imagery when it investigated physical damage to US bases in the region, verified with help from a lower-resolution European science satellite
🔴 US satellite firms are publicly traded, with the Pentagon among their biggest customers - creating a powerful commercial incentive to heed government wishes.
Israel's special treatment is where it gets interesting:
Since 1997, US law has required American satellite imagery providers to keep the resolution of Israeli imagery deliberately below a certain threshold. Israel remains the only country granted this legal protection.
The blurred difference is visible even on public tools like Google Earth.
👉 For decades, this has complicated not only the monitoring of[ Israel's devastating war in Gaza](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/73195), where Israel has banned foreign journalists since 2023, but also the expansion of [illegal settlements in the West Bank.](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/73789O)
An Oregon State University study using European Sentinel-1 data found that over three-fifths of all buildings in Gaza were damaged or destroyed in the first year of the war.
➡️ In Iran, when the [US bombed a school in Minab](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/73701), killing an estimated 168 civilians, including 120 children - the Pentagon initially denied responsibility. The New York Times [used satellite images to confirm a US Tomahawk missile](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/66575) [was most likely responsible ](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/65634)
Incidentally, the proposed 2027 Intelligence Authorization Act seeks to codify restrictions that would bar (or tightly control) public release of sensitive imagery by US government-contracted providers when such release “could harm national security” - a definition broad enough to be abused.

The Purge Factor

Sending them all back to Quantico sends a message: "I'm in charge. You'll either fall in line or fall out."
